output.interpretation: Two-group comparison: human pancreatic cancer (PDAC) cell lines grown in 2D/3D culture and treated with a direct KRAS inhibitor (case: e.g. MRTX1133 for KRAS G12D, sotorasib/adagrasib for KRAS G12C, or a pan-KRAS inhibitor such as BI-2865) versus the same cell line given vehicle (DMSO) for the same length of time (control). Within each series the comparison should be matched by cell line and time point. Combination-drug arms, drug-resistant derived lines, xenografts, organoids and mouse lines are excluded. I could not open the GEO records (NCBI returned a reCAPTCHA page), so none of the sample lists below have been checked, and GSM accessions are left empty rather than guessed.

clarifying_questions.question: Should RAS(ON) multi-selective tri-complex inhibitors (RMC-6236/daraxonrasib, RMC-7977) count as a 'direct KRAS inhibitor', or only KRAS-selective drugs (MRTX1133, sotorasib, adagrasib, BI-2865-type pan-KRAS)?
options: Also include RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitors such as RMC-6236
clarifying_questions.why: GSE314456 (PSN1 and SW1990 treated with RMC-6236 vs DMSO) qualifies only if pan-RAS(ON) inhibitors are accepted.

clarifying_questions.question: Should the case arm be limited to one KRAS allele and drug, or pool all direct KRAS inhibitors across cell lines?
options: Any direct KRAS inhibitor, with cell line as a covariate
clarifying_questions.why: Most available series use MRTX1133 in G12D lines (AsPC-1, PANC-1, SW1990, HPAC). G12C/sotorasib data in MIA PaCa-2 are scarce and mostly compare resistant with parental cells.

clarifying_questions.question: Which treatment duration should be used when a series has more than one time point?
options: Short (≤24 h, direct KRAS-ERK target genes)
Any, matched with vehicle at the same time
clarifying_questions.why: Early time points show direct KRAS/ERK targets (DUSP6, SPRY4, ETV4/5, FOSL1, MYC). Later time points add cell-cycle and feedback effects. The answer decides which samples in a multi-time-point series are used.

Each cell line is analysed separately, or blocked by line.
